key_insight: Neural-network models applied to text embeddings of online news can produce scalable, cross-dataset measures of national "peace" and the same AI methods can power online tools that help users understand and improve their media diet to promote peace.
problem_solved: Provides a data-driven, reproducible way to measure levels of peace from large-scale news and social media and addresses the lack of user-facing tools that make media consumption’s impact on peace understandable and actionable.
method: Compute text embeddings from online news sources and train neural networks to predict country-level peace indicators from those embeddings.
Demonstrate cross-dataset generalization: a model trained on one news corpus retained high accuracy when evaluated on a different news dataset.
Extend the approach to social platforms (e.g., YouTube) and build online visualization/education tools that reveal users’ media diets and suggest peace-promoting changes.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a validated pipeline for measuring societal signals (peace) from text and a blueprint for turning those signals into user-facing interventions—useful for research, policy monitoring, and peace-focused products.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data sources → text embedding → neural network → country peace score → user tool

paper_title: Measuring and Fostering Peace through Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
paper_authors: P. Gilda, P. Dungarwal, A. Thongkham, E. T. Ajayi, S. Choudhary
